5458.title: Use pinned Alpine CDN package for native bootstrap (#5414)
5458.body:
[Native/Alpine] Bootstrap from a pinned Alpine CDN package (#5414)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4013
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3112792
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1645006
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1645300

Remove the GitLab generic-package endpoint from Alpine cross-image
bootstrap. October 22 public and internal builds failed before native
compilation while connecting to gitlab.alpinelinux.org:443. One internal
x64 download spent approximately 852 seconds exhausting six attempts.
The same main commit had downloaded and checksum-verified the artifact
successfully on October 20. DNS resolved during investigation, but HTTPS
connections also timed out from the developer machine, including forced
IPv4; this was not confined to 1ES. The exact server or routing fault
remains unconfirmed.

The earlier retry fix in #4013 handled transient GitLab HTTP 500 responses,
but retries cannot repair sustained endpoint unavailability. Use Alpine's
reachable package-distribution CDN instead of its GitLab package registry.
Replace the standalone apk.static 2.12.14 download with the exact
apk-tools-static-2.14.6-r3.apk archive from the existing v3.21/main/x86_64
repository, and pin its SHA-256 before extracting sbin/apk.static.
The x86_64 executable runs on the cross-build host; APK_ARCH continues to
select the target sysroot rather than the bootstrap tool architecture.

Retain curl's HTTP failure detection and five retries, adding a 20-second
connection timeout and 120-second transfer limit per attempt. Preserve
signed fontconfig-dev installation and the explicit Azure Linux CA-bundle
path. Missing artifacts and checksum mismatches stop the build; do not
probe alternate tools or bypass verification. Document updating the exact
package version and archive checksum together. These pins constrain the
bootstrap artifact, not the versions resolved from Alpine's package feeds.

Validation independently verified the embedded executable's Alpine
RSA-SHA256 signature, exercised signed fontconfig-dev installation for
x64, arm, arm64, riscv64 and loongarch64, and rejected both a wrong checksum
and an unavailable package. Public build 1645300 tested head d96d97a4baf
through its PR merge ref and passed the ten Alpine native jobs, covering
those five architectures with and without nodeps. Its x64 image log shows
an actual archive download and successful checksum verification, not a
cached bootstrap layer. The overall run failed in the non-Alpine Linux
x86 job; the Alpine results do not imply a green pipeline.



(cherry picked from commit 48e2083869ab2b154b2058c32682391d1c77e403)

5286.title: [skia-sync] Pin m155 servicing fixes
5286.body:
[skia-sync] Pin m155 servicing fixes (#5286)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/394
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/6a3f259016481f7b5ce70bb7f511fd79c3005458...5b289b73e698a7d2f1162d535332987c080289c1

Advance the 4.155 release line to the reviewed and merged chrome/m155
servicing fixes. Pin externals/skia and cgmanifest.json to mono/skia
merge commit 5b289b73e698a7d2f1162d535332987c080289c1 and record
upstream commit 29ed1e87a0a50f3d8347e988842d9d59e7573efa.

The native merge contains reviewed commit
8442e6c3d66775892df16c6eb2b663c991ce50d1 and has the identical
tree. Repinning preserves its upstream ancestry without changing the
reviewed native content. This is a same-milestone sync: package versions,
native ABI, managed APIs, and generated bindings remain unchanged.

~~ Ganesh cache entries after a failed flush ~~

A failed render task can publish a cache entry for a texture that was
never initialized. The native update drops uniquely held thread-safe
cache entries after a failed flush so later draws cannot reuse them.
The updated native test distinguishes the cleared view entry from the
unaffected vertex entry.

~~ FontConfig first-candidate matching ~~

Scanning past the first valid font could accept a lower-ranked
metric-compatible substitute instead of letting the caller try the
next requested family. The native update tests family acceptability
only on the first valid sorted candidate and adds a regression test.

The corrected native head removes a fork-only validity guard from the
direct FcFontMatch path, leaving the full FontConfig file identical to
the recorded upstream version. Corrected-head Linux source build and
unfiltered managed tests passed, and fresh regeneration matched all
five binding configurations. The full Windows build remained blocked
by missing Windows SDK 10.0.19041.0.

5162.title: Disable RAW and DNG image decoding
5162.body:
Disable RAW and DNG image decoding (#5162)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/373
Changes: https://github.com/mono/skia/compare/19c623188a14c42daec09c7e3d5ac74b43c2d916...cd9ab17d2dc927ec647b897d5e3e3b997dc9a05a

Retire the bundled RAW decoding path rather than continue supporting
Adobe's DNG SDK. Align codec availability, samples, and downloaded
dependencies while preserving the public API.

~~ Retire RAW decoding without removing public API ~~

Set skia_use_dng_sdk=false and skia_use_piex=false in GenerateGnBuild,
replacing the platform-specific flags with a shared policy. This disables
both DNG development and PIEX-based embedded JPEG preview decoding.
WASM already disabled these features.

The previous RAW path preferred a usable JPEG preview over developing
the RAW data. Such a preview can have lower resolution and already-baked
processing; retaining PIEX alone would provide previews, not full RAW
development. No replacement decoder is introduced here. The PR records
PIEX-only, Apple Core Image, and Skia-focused Rust alternatives for reference.

Keep SKEncodedImageFormat.Dng = 10 for source and binary compatibility,
and document that the enum value does not imply codec support. Remove
the unsupported Gallery choice and the DNG-only Alpine __WORDSIZE
workaround.

Move the existing Gallery DNG file unchanged into test content. The
regression verifies null results from codec, bitmap, and image decoding,
with Unimplemented reported by the file and managed-stream codec paths.
The local unfiltered net10.0 console suite and Gallery shared build passed.

~~ Stop fetching unused RAW dependencies ~~

Disabling GN codec flags does not stop tools/git-sync-deps from fetching
entries in DEPS. Consume the companion native change that comments out
dng_sdk and piex, and remove their Component Governance registrations
and active-dependency documentation.

Point both the submodule and its manifest registration at native merge
cd9ab17d2dc927ec647b897d5e3e3b997dc9a05a. Its tree is identical to reviewed
commit a77114f665011831f9a2cf98f9f56806f2fc1089, preserving the native
source used for validation.

Dependency synchronization and the macOS ARM64 native build succeeded
with both downloaded source directories absent, without recreating them.
The dependency-metadata reconciliation tests also passed.

Existing local dependency directories, upstream codec sources, and the
unused upstream Bazel configuration are not deleted or rewritten.

Co-authored-by: Matthew Leibowitz <mattleibow@live.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

5146.title: [CI] Route public Apple jobs to AcesShared and Xcode 26.3
5146.body:
[CI] Route public Apple jobs to AcesShared and Xcode 26.3 (#5146)

Move the public native and managed Apple lanes off the backed-up hosted
macOS queue and use the same Xcode 26.3 baseline in both paths. This
replaces the native Xcode 16.2 exception while retaining the existing
Apple build topology.

~~ Route public macOS work through AcesShared ~~

`buildAgentMac` and `buildAgentMacNative` previously used `Azure Pipelines`
with `vmImage: macos-15`. Route both through `AcesShared` with
`ImageOverride -equals ACES_VM_SharedPool_Sequoia` so the native Apple stage
and managed macOS leg share the public pool selection.

Build 1606244 completed its `Native macOS` stage after the new pool's
authorization checkpoint, including its iOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, and tvOS
jobs. This validates the routing after the public pipeline received access
to the pool.

~~ Align native Apple builds with Xcode 26.3 ~~

The bootstrapper selects `XCODE_VERSION_NATIVE` for `native_` jobs and
`XCODE_VERSION` for other macOS jobs. Native compilation had therefore
remained on 16.2 while managed work used 26.3. Set the native variable to
26.3 so the two paths no longer select different compiler baselines.

Source builds of the pinned Skia revision succeeded for `externals-ios`,
`externals-maccatalyst`, `externals-macos`, and `externals-tvos` with local
Xcode 26.6. That proves source compatibility with the Xcode 26 line, not
an exact reproduction of an uncached AcesShared 26.3 build.

The unfiltered `net10.0` test run passed 6,328 tests and skipped 23 but
reported one macOS Ganesh GL `DiagonalLines` visual-golden mismatch. A
focused 25-test visual-matrix rerun reproduced it; the source build, not
the visual result, is the compiler-compatibility evidence for this change.

5135.title: Update harfbuzz to 14.4.0
5135.body:
Update HarfBuzz to 14.4.0 (#5135)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/370
Changes: https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz/compare/14.2.1...14.4.0
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/cbb18261-c48f-4abb-8651-8cdcb5474649/_build/results?buildId=1606372

Update the native dependency, package identity, and generated interop surface
together so HarfBuzzSharp consumes HarfBuzz 14.4 without publishing
native-shaped helper methods as managed API.

~~ Native HarfBuzz 14.4 integration ~~

Advance HarfBuzz from 14.2.1 commit
56feae4035bdd48f62ba2b8d8c16232d4d89b3a4 to 14.4.0 commit
36cb489cb02ce4b92099669ba9f9bea348eff93f through the merged mono/skia
companion.

Reconcile Skia's explicit GN inventory with the new release. Add the OpenType
dependency-graph and raw-value fetch sources. Remove the empty
hb-raster.cc and hb-subset-cff2-to-cff1.cc translation units, which upstream
deleted because GCC LTO could leak filename-derived weak symbols from them.
Raster and CFF2 conversion implementations remain in their other translation
units.

Refresh the Component Governance identity and set the native release and
soname to 14.4.0 and 0.61440.0. Reset the HarfBuzzSharp package versions from
14.2.1.500 to 14.4.0 because a new native release starts a new package revision
line.

Point both the submodule gitlink and its Component Governance registration at
mono/skia merge commit 19c623188a14c42daec09c7e3d5ac74b43c2d916. Its tree
9795ad92a7dbc05c5eaa8cae73c0ef8c77d2e0f8 is identical to the reviewed native
commit, preserving the source validated by the companion PR.

The upstream range includes intentional shaping-output changes to
cross-direction mark positioning for DirectWrite and Core Text compatibility,
glyph-position saturation, malformed-font crash and hang fixes, and subsetting
and shaping performance work. The macOS ARM64 native source build and the
manually queued mono-SkiaSharp Azure build 1606372 completed successfully.

~~ Generated HarfBuzzSharp API boundary ~~

HarfBuzz 14.3 added raw OpenType bits and number fetch APIs, and HarfBuzz 14.4
added set intersection. Regenerate internal bindings for
hb_ot_fetch_bits(), hb_ot_fetch_number(), and hb_set_intersects(), and map the
usable native tag values to the documented public OpenTypeBitsTag and
OpenTypeNumberTag enums while suppressing their native maximum sentinels.

Keep the raw functions internal and introduce no Face wrappers. This avoids
committing the public API to native-shaped signatures so future managed
wrappers can provide value-adding names and behavior instead of merely
mirroring the C API.

The Linux, Windows, and macOS generation checks and generated-binding
comparison passed. The enum documentation is present in compiler-produced
HarfBuzzSharp.xml, the package XML documentation contract passed, and the
canonical net10.0 test solution completed with zero failures.

5153.title: [release] Detect stale transition sync pull requests
5153.body:
[release] Detect stale transition sync pull requests (#5153)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5081
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5141
Context: https://github.com/mono/skia/pull/371

Prevent servicing-line audits from losing an open milestone sync when main
advances and the old line moves to release/A.B.x.

After m155 landed, Get-ExpectedSyncBranch correctly changed the expected m154
head from skia-sync/m154 to skia-sync/release-4.154.x. The audit then queried
only that exact head/base pair. The reciprocal m154 PRs remained open against
main and skiasharp but disappeared from the 4.154 report, allowing it to report
the servicing upstream state as current without surfacing the stale pair.

For servicing lines, also query the pre-transition skia-sync/mN head against
the servicing and former main-line bases in both repositories. Only open pull
requests activate this fallback, so abandoned branch refs do not create
phantom release work.

Route a discovered pair through the existing head, gitlink, and base
validation. If either PR still targets main or skiasharp, report the pair as
inconsistent retarget-or-close work and block the release cut. Give that
inconsistent result precedence over a normal draft servicing PR; when the
legacy pair is fully retargeted, preserve the normal servicing result.

Live validation now reports SkiaSharp #5141 and mono/skia#371 for 4.154. The
native PR tree matches the m154 servicing merge already landed, while the
parent differs only in its cgmanifest and submodule pointers, confirming that
this particular pair is superseded and should be closed. The publishing suite
passes all 279 tests, including the coexisting normal and stale PR case.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

[skia-sync] Update Skia to milestone 155 (#5081)

Advance SkiaSharp from Chrome milestone 154 to 155 using the reviewed and

release/4.154.x and move main to the 4.155 package and native ABI line.

~~ Advance the milestone line ~~

bf34df08cd99e9436a20e82f17d01c89d94d1a3a.

5138.title: [release] Create missing shipped milestones automatically
5138.body:
[release] Create missing shipped milestones automatically (#5138)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/35395494383

Make Release - Finish and standalone Release - Milestones recover when an
exact shipped-release milestone does not exist. Preserve the existing safety
checks for missing tags, release boundaries, and ambiguous ownership.

~~ Repair missing shipped milestones ~~

Release assignment reconciliation previously converted an absent target
milestone into a warning and skipped its assignments. During Finish, this could
fail the required milestone job after the public package, immutable tag, and
GitHub Release already existed.

Project the missing milestone into dry-run planning and report its creation
without calling GitHub. Keep dependent assignments symbolic instead of
printing a PATCH with the virtual negative milestone number.

During push, create and verify the milestone before calculating assignments,
then use its actual GitHub number for pull requests and linked issues. Existing
milestones remain unchanged, and the normal milestone-update step can close
the new milestone after reconciliation.

~~ Share milestone creation semantics ~~

Add New-GitHubMilestone to Publishing.Common and use it for both shipped-release
repair and scheduled milestone creation. This keeps title, description, due
date, dry-run output, and post-write verification under one contract instead
of constructing milestone POST requests in multiple scripts.

Treat HTTP 422 as a possible concurrent creator rather than immediate failure.
Refresh the complete milestone map and continue only when the exact unique
title now exists; otherwise preserve the original failure. Duplicate milestone
titles remain rejected by Get-GitHubMilestoneMap.

The milestone suite passes 72 tests and the publishing contract suite passes
269 tests, including dry-run projection, symbolic assignment output,
idempotency, concurrent creation recovery, shared-helper reuse, and production
call ordering.
